note: Every info bite in 90 Day Quest must cite one of these. Each entry was checked against the paper or publisher page on 2026-10-27.

sources.cite: Lally, van Jaarsveld, Potts & Wardle (2010). How are habits formed: Modelling habit formation in the real world. European Journal of Social Psychology, 40, 998-1009.
sources.verified: 82 of 96 participants analysed; median time to 95% of automaticity asymptote 66 days, range 18-254 (model fit for 39); missing one opportunity did not materially affect habit formation.

sources.cite: Gollwitzer & Sheeran (2006). Implementation intentions and goal achievement: A meta-analysis of effects and processes. Advances in Experimental Social Psychology, 38, 69-119.
sources.verified: 94 independent tests; d = 0.65 on goal attainment.

sources.cite: Harkin et al. (2016). Does monitoring goal progress promote goal attainment? A meta-analysis of the experimental evidence. Psychological Bulletin, 142(2), 198-229.
sources.verified: 138 studies, 19,951 participants; monitoring improved attainment d = 0.40; larger when physically recorded or reported publicly.

sources.cite: Wood & Runger (2016). Psychology of habit. Annual Review of Psychology, 67.
sources.verified: Context cues automatically activate habitual responses; habits build on rewarded responses being repeated.

sources.cite: Dai, Milkman & Riis (2014). The fresh start effect: Temporal landmarks motivate aspirational behavior. Management Science.
sources.verified: Gym visit probability +33.4% at new week, +47.1% at new semester.

sources.cite: Kivetz, Urminsky & Zheng (2006). The goal-gradient hypothesis resurrected. Journal of Marketing Research, 43, 39-58.
sources.verified: 12-stamp card with 2 pre-filled completed faster (12.7 vs 15.6 days) than plain 10-stamp card.

sources.cite: Bull et al. (2020). World Health Organization 2020 guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behaviour. British Journal of Sports Medicine, 54, 1451-1462.
sources.verified: Adults: 150-300 min moderate or 75-150 min vigorous per week; regular muscle strengthening; some activity better than none.

sources.cite: Paluch et al. (2022). Daily steps and all-cause mortality: a meta-analysis of 15 international cohorts. Lancet Public Health, 7, e219-28.
sources.verified: 47,471 adults; risk levelled off ~6,000-8,000 steps (60+) and ~8,000-10,000 (<60); top vs bottom quartile HR 0.47.

sources.cite: Burke, Wang & Sevick (2011). Self-monitoring in weight loss: a systematic review of the literature. Journal of the American Dietetic Association, 111(1), 92-102.
sources.verified: 22 studies; consistent significant association between self-monitoring and weight loss; evidence level rated weak due to methods.

sources.cite: Morton et al. (2018). A systematic review, meta-analysis and meta-regression of the effect of protein supplementation on resistance training-induced gains in muscle mass and strength in healthy adults. British Journal of Sports Medicine, 52(6), 376-384.
sources.verified: 49 RCTs, 1,863 participants; +0.30 kg fat-free mass, +2.49 kg 1RM; no further gains beyond ~1.62 g/kg/day (95% CI 1.03-2.20).

sources.cite: Watson et al. (2015). Recommended amount of sleep for a healthy adult: a joint consensus statement of the AASM and SRS. Journal of Clinical Sleep Medicine, 11(6), 591-592.
sources.verified: Adults should sleep 7 or more hours per night on a regular basis.
